title: The search box that suggested a person
blurb: Raw prefixes got cached and one-off queries trended.
prompt: A private individual's name appeared in autocomplete after one search and then stayed cached, because the draft cached raw prefixes forever and promoted single-occurrence queries as trends. The same endpoint returned thousands of matches for long prefixes. Review it, fix it, and prove caches are capped and trends have floors.
aiNote: The draft caches every prefix with no TTL or cap, so a single sensitive query becomes a permanent suggestion, and the trending path has no occurrence floor or sensitive-category filter, turning one search into a global trend.
testIdea: Walk ten thousand distinct prefixes and assert the cache cap evicts oldest while memory stays bounded; search a one-off term and assert it never trends without the floor; assert a cached prefix expires with its TTL.
followUps: What occurrence floor makes a trend defensible?
How do you keep typeahead useful under cache caps?
